newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian statement warns of "bloody future".
newsitem.headline: Algerian statement warns of "bloody future".

text.p: An Algerian Islamist group calling itself The Faithful of the Sermon said in a statement on Monday Algeria's future would be "more bloody and the earth will tremble under the feet of the tyrannical regime".

In the statement sent to an international news agency, the group said it controlled zones in Algeria and that a nationwide speech on "terrorism" by Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Friday showed his "regime" was near its end.
It was not possible to check the authenticity of the statement which mixed verses from the Moslem holy book, the Koran, with accusations against the Algerian authorities.
The statement accused the authorities of carrying out massacres of civilians with the aim of both discrediting the "holy war" warriors, and disguising military defeats.

Algeria has been in conflict since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS). About 60,000 people have since died, including about 250 since the January 10 start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.

Early in the conflict, a political group calling itself by a similar name made several political statements. These were signed by one of the sons of Abassi Madani, the jailed leader of the FIS. But there has been no evidence of any armed group of that name operating in Algeria.
The most feared group is the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) which took up arms after the armed wing of the FIS, the Islamic Salvation Army (AIS), dominated the early conflict.
